newsitem.title: USA: US continues SmithKline Beecham probe -Reno.
newsitem.headline: US continues SmithKline Beecham probe -Reno.

text.p: U.S. Justice Department officials said Monday a criminal probe of SmithKline Beecham Plc's clinical laboratory unit continued even though it reached a $325 million civil settlement over alleged false claims filed with government.
"All I can say is that the investigation continues," Attorney General Janet Reno said when asked about possible criminal charges at a Justice Department news conference.

In London earlier Monday, the company announced the settlement under which SmithKline Beecham will pay $325 million to resolve the U.S. government's civil and administrative claims against the company.

Chief Executive Jan Leschly said the problem stemmed from ambiguities in regulations and guidelines, and the decision to settle did not mean the company had intentionally violated any laws. He said the settlement decision "was driven by the enormous potential costs and uncertainties connected with lengthy litigation."

The settlement involved allegations the unit, based in Collegeville, Pa., had performed tests that were not needed or ordered by physicians under federal health care programs and had billed for certain tests that were not performed.

U.S. Attorney Michael Stiles in Philadelphia, a federal prosecutor who helped negotiate the agreement, said in a statement the civil settlement "does not resolve any potential criminal charges" against the lab unit or any individuals.
